assessments.reasoning: Sections 15 and 18.2.5 support the printed modifier order. The §15.3 result example and the §18.5 Project sequence comprehension preserve projected occurrences, but the immediately adjacent §18.5 cardinality equality says the output mapping has the cardinality of that same mapping in the input. The equality conflicts with the exact narrower-domain case this proposal expressly includes.

challenge.method: Recompute the exact printed Project comprehension and its separately printed equality for two distinct mappings with the same projected variable value and different removed-variable values. Compare the published 1.1 errata and the successor W3C issue 80, its linked pull request and the dated 1.2 Working Draft.
challenge.results: The two input mappings become two identical reduced-domain output mappings under the comprehension. Neither input is the reduced-domain mapping, so the literal equality assigns that output key zero occurrences. The successor issue labels the defect a confirmed erratum via its label description and the later draft changelog records a Project-cardinality fix. These contextual records do not amend the dated 2013 text. The no-ORDER-BY condition avoids a separate ordering issue but does not repair this contradiction.

limitations: The exact r1 conjunct about occurrence preservation remains adverse. A separately authored revision can scope the modifier ordering and duplicate elimination language to the literal §15 and §18.2.5 statements. This assessment supplies no corrected normative Project formula or applicability to other editions.
